title: Prove zero-preserving polynomial helpers cannot reduce linear call minima (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with finite exact corroboration. Grant a labelled linear-operator call a free coordinatewise polynomial before or after it, with every polynomial fixing zero. For an exact linear endpoint over an infinite field, this extension has the same Pareto-minimal operator-call profiles as the linear model, including all required dirty and clean returns.

```text
b += p(Ta)  or  b += T p(a)
              |
              | extract degree one at the common zero state
              v
b += p'(0) T a
zero derivative: delete call; otherwise keep operator, ports, label and order
```

Scalar multiplication by p'(0) must belong to the comparison's permitted linear class. The classical degree-one quotient/chain rule proves the extraction. The new contribution is the explicit helper-interface profile statement, its uniform-family corollary and its bounded executable extractor. Produced by Nick Petalas. No predecessor scientific replay is the deliverable, no literature-priority claim is made, and no new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Only `research/polynomial-helper-profile-domination/` is added. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19228481). The delivered scope matches that claim.

## Evidence

Before, a linear operator-call obstruction leaves zero-preserving nonlinear data-value processing unspecified. After, every exact linear endpoint in this polynomial class supplies a linear word whose count in each label class is no larger.

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64 passes `PASS_POLYNOMIAL_HELPER_PROFILE_DOMINATION`:

- 145 complete sparse-polynomial endpoint and inverse fixtures, including clean and arbitrary dirty returns, singular/nonsymmetric rational operators, both placements and successive noncommuting blocks.
- 1,029 directions each for a separate dual-number interpreter and literal rational execution, with 14 invalid-input or essential-boundary controls. These finite checks corroborate the written theorem.
- Registered warning-strict normal and optimized replay, syntax/function-size inspection, metadata/source pins and exact committed-byte/source-history preflight pass. Each registered argv was timed locally, 0.219 and 0.216 seconds, below its 120-second timeout. These are replay-budget measurements, not a performance claim.
- Official committed export integrity/input-coverage checks and a read-only, Git-free optimized replay pass.
- The five-gate dirty echo's illustrative labelled profile goes from `T:3, read:2` to `T:2, read:2`. These abstract labels are not measured Fourier ranks or selected-word jobs. The generated receipt binds all seven proof/code/metadata sources by SHA256.

From the worktree root, exact reproduction commands:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/polynomial-helper-profile-domination/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/polynomial-helper-profile-domination/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/polynomial-helper-profile-domination
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/polynomial-helper-profile-domination --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local interpreter path. No third-party dependencies are needed. The theorem has no polynomial degree or finite-workspace-count bound across different candidate words; the rational implementation enforces its separately documented finite bounds.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This is an optimistic labelled operator-call model. Actual scalar, frame, native, tape, precision, stock and compiler costs are not equated or supplied. The extractor does not certify that its input word's endpoint is linear; the verifier separately establishes that premise on the fixtures. Nonzero constant trajectories, branching, finite-grid/rounded execution, nonlinear address permutations and nonlinear output contracts are outside the theorem.

No selected-word replay, physical supplier, full multiplication theorem, Lean or Docker check was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml's #1757 nonlinear finite-alphabet cut theorem and Chris R / Clear1nsight's #3992 typed Toom/Jacobian obstruction are credited and pinned context, not audited here.

## Related open work

- #6015 studies a data-dependent finite menu of fixed linear endpoint maps. This PR instead fixes one nonlinear arithmetic word and extracts its linear endpoint; neither result supplies the other's premise or a new selected supplier.
- #5944 prices a nonlinear finite-alphabet six-frame circuit through two cut partitions. This PR has an infinite-field polynomial gate contract and a different operator-call price; its conclusion does not extend that finite-alphabet exclusion.

## Open next questions

- Can a nonzero constant trajectory yield a cheaper complete helper word? First price the constants, coordinate-dependent derivatives, retained outputs and restoration. The translated-square boundary witness only shows where this proof stops.
- Can a finite-grid polynomial or bit-operation mechanism save calls under an exact selected-source precision contract? First specify the grid, nonlinear consumer and arbitrary dirty inputs. The F2 square control prevents transferring this derivative theorem to finite grids.
